aligned.ja: ומתו בו כי יחללוהו, וקאל פי אלטבל ולא יחללו את קדשי בני ישראל, פכמא אלחלול אלמד'כור פי אלתרומה במיתה כד'לך אלחלול אלמד'כור פי אלטבל. וזר שאכל תרומה לאן בעד קולה ומתו בו כי יחללוהו קאל וכל זר לא יאכל קדש. וזר ששמש בביאן והזר הקרב יומת. וטמא ששמש מן קולה פי אלטמאים וינזרו מקדשי בני ישראל ולא יחללו. והד'א אלחלול מת'ל אלחלול אלמד'כור פי קולה ומתו בו כי יחללוהו.
aligned.en: [The following completes the close of Chapter Nine; it is not part of *Ḥeleq* itself.] As for one who is impure and ate pure *terumah*, [his liability to death by Heaven] derives from the verse "and they shall die for it if they profane it" (Leviticus 22:9); and concerning one who eats untithed produce (*tevel*) Scripture says, "and they shall not profane the holy things of the Children of Israel" (Leviticus 22:15) — so that just as the "profanation" mentioned in connection with *terumah* carries death, so too the "profanation" mentioned in connection with untithed produce. And [the same applies to] a non-priest who ate *terumah*, for after the verse "and they shall die for it if they profane it" Scripture says, "no non-priest shall eat of a holy thing" (Leviticus 22:10). A non-priest who performed [Temple] service [incurs death], as is made plain by "and the non-priest who draws near shall be put to death" (Numbers 18:7). An impure person who performed service [derives his liability] from the verse concerning the impure, "that they separate themselves from the holy things of the Children of Israel and not profane [them]" (Leviticus 22:2–3) — and this "profanation" is like the "profanation" mentioned in "and they shall die for it if they profane it."

pairs.en: "and they shall die for it if they profane it"

aligned.ja: וטבול יום נקל מסנוד לקולה קדשים יהיו לאלהיהם ולא יחללו. ומחוסר בגדים לקולה פי אלכהנים וחגרת אותם אבנט אהרן ובניו וכו', בזמן שבגדיהן עליהן כהונתן עליהן, אמא אד'א נקץ מנהא שי פהו כזר. ומחוסר כפורים לקולה וכפר עליה הכהן וטהרה דליל אן קבל הבאת כפרה טמאה תתסמי, וקד צח אן לא עבודה לטמא, ואם עבד במיתה.
aligned.en: One who immersed that day [but had not yet waited until nightfall, the *tevul yom*,] is derived by tradition resting upon the verse "they shall be holy to their God and shall not profane [it]" (Leviticus 21:6). One lacking [the requisite priestly] garments [is derived] from the verse concerning the priests, "and you shall gird them with sashes, Aaron and his sons" (Exodus 29:9) — for while their garments are upon them their priesthood is upon them, but if anything of them is missing he is like a non-priest. One still lacking [the requisite] atonement [offerings, the *meḥusar kippurim*, is derived] from "and the priest shall make atonement for her and she shall be clean" (Leviticus 12:8), which proves that before bringing her atonement she is called impure; and it is established that an impure person performs no [valid] service, and if he performed service he incurs death.

aligned.ja: ושלא רחוץ ידים ורגלים בביאן ירחצו מים ולא ימותו. יין ושכר אל תשת וכו'. ראשיכם אל תפרעו ובגדיכם לא תפרומו ולא תמותו. ואין הלכה כר' עקיבה.
aligned.en: And [the prohibition against serving] without having washed hands and feet is made plain by "they shall wash with water, that they die not" (Exodus 30:20–21). [And concerning those who drank wine,] "Wine and strong drink you shall not drink" etc. (Leviticus 10:9). [And concerning those with disheveled hair and torn garments,] "Do not let the hair of your heads grow long, nor rend your garments, that you die not" (Leviticus 10:6). And the law is not in accordance with R. Akiva.

aligned.ja: אעלם אן אהל אלשריעה אכ'תלפת אראהם פי אלסעאדה אלתי ינאלהא אלאנסאן באמתת'אל הד'ה אלשראיע אלתי שרענא אללה בהא עלי ידי משה רבינו, ופי אלשקאוה אלתי תלחקנא ענד אלתעדי עליהא אכ'תלאפא כת'ירא ג'דא עלי חסב אכ'תלאף אלעקול, ותשושת פי ד'לך אלאד'האן תשושא כת'ירא, חתי אנך יכאד לא תג'ד בוג'ה שכ'צא צפי לה הד'א אלבאב, נעם ולא תג'ד פיה כלאמא מרסלא לאחד אלא עלי תשויש כת'יר.
aligned.en: Know that the people of the [revealed] Law have differed greatly in their views concerning the felicity that a person attains by fulfilling these commandments which God prescribed for us through Moses our Teacher, and concerning the misery that overtakes us when we transgress them — they have differed exceedingly, in accordance with the differences of their intellects, and over this their minds have fallen into great confusion. Indeed, you will scarcely find anyone at all for whom this matter has been clarified, nor will you find on it any well-ordered discourse from anyone, except amid much confusion.

pairs.en: the people of the [revealed] Law

aligned.ja: פטאיפה תעתקד אן אלסעאדה אנמא הי גן עדן, ואנה מוצ'ע יוכל פיה וישרב דון שקא ג'סם דון תעב, ואן יכון פיה ביות מן אחג'אר עאליה ומנאבר חריר, ואנהאר תג'רי מן כ'מר ואדהאן טיבה, וכת'יר מן הד'א אלנוע. ואן אלשקאוה גהנם, ואנה מוצ'ע מאג'ג' נארא תחרק פיה אלג'ת'ת' ויתעד'ב אלנאס פיה אנואע מן אלעד'אב יטול שרחהא. ותסתדל הד'ה אלטאיפה עלי הד'א אלאעתקאד באקואל כת'ירה מן אקואל אלחכמים עליהם אלסלאם תטאבק לעמרך ט'ואהרהא דעואהם או אכת'ר.
aligned.en: One group holds that the felicity [in question] is the Garden of Eden, and that it is a place where one eats and drinks without bodily toil and without exertion, where there are houses of precious stones and couches of silk, and rivers that run with wine and fragrant oils, and much of this kind. And [they hold] that the misery is Gehinnom, a place that blazes with fire in which the corpses are burned and where people are tormented with kinds of torments too long to describe. This group adduces support for this belief from many sayings of the Sages, may peace be upon them, whose plain sense — by your life — agrees with their claim, or with most of it.

pairs.en: the felicity [in question] is the Garden of Eden

aligned.ja: וטאיפה ת'אניה תעתקד ותט'ן אן אלסעאדה אלמתרג'אה אנמא הי ימות המשיח מהרה יגלה, ואן ד'לך אלזמאן יכון אלנאס כלהם מלוך דאימין ותעט'ם ג'ת'ת'הם ויעמרון אלארץ' כלהא אלי אלאבד, וד'לך אלמשיח בזעמהם יעיש מא דאם אלבארי ג'ל ת'נאוה, ואן פי ד'לך אלזמאן תנבת אלארץ' ת'יאב מנסוג'ה וכ'בז מכ'בוז וממתנעאת כת'ירה מת'ל הד'ה. ואלשקאוה הי אן לא יכון אלאנסאן פי ד'לך אלזמאן ולא יזכי למשאהדתה, ויסתדלון איצ'א עלי ד'לך באקואל כת'ירה מוג'ודה לאלחכמים ובנצוץ מן אלמקרא יואפק ט'ואהרהא דעואהם או בעצ'ה.
aligned.en: A second group holds and supposes that the hoped-for felicity is the days of the Messiah — may he be revealed speedily — and that in that age all people will be everlasting kings, their bodies will grow mighty, and they will inhabit the whole earth forever; and that this Messiah, by their reckoning, will live as long as the Creator, may His praise be exalted, endures; and that in that age the earth will bring forth woven garments and baked bread and many such impossible things. And the misery [on their view] is that a person should not be alive in that age and should not merit to behold it. They too adduce support for this from many sayings found among the Sages, and from verses of Scripture whose plain sense agrees with their claim, or with part of it.

aligned.ja: וטאיפה ת'אלת'ה תזעם אן אלסעאדה אלמתרג'אה הי אחיא אלאמואת, וד'לך אן יעיש אלאנסאן בעד מותה וירג'ע מע אהלה וקראבתה יאכל וישרב ולא ימות אכת'ר. ואלשקאוה אן לא יעיש, ויסתדלון איצ'א עלי הד'א באקאול לאלחכמים ובבעץ' פואסק פי אלנצוץ תטבאק הד'א אלדעוי.
aligned.en: A third group maintains that the hoped-for felicity is the resurrection of the dead — that is, that a person should live again after his death and return among his family and kin, eating and drinking and never dying again. And the misery is that he should not live again. They too adduce support for this from sayings of the Sages and from a few passages in Scripture whose plain sense agrees with this claim.

aligned.en: A fourth group maintains that the felicity we attain by fulfilling the commandments is bodily ease and worldly aspirations in this world — such as the fertility of the land, abundance of wealth and children, length of days, soundness of body, security, having a king from among us, and our holding dominion over those who have been our enemies. And [they hold] that the misery that overtakes us when we transgress is the contrary of all these conditions — as is in fact our state in this present age, the age of the exile. They adduce support, by their reckoning, from all the verses of the Torah concerning the blessings and the curses and the like, and from the whole of the narratives recorded in Scripture.

You will not find anyone at all asking about this or discoursing upon it.

aligned.en: Now you, sir, grasp this parable from me, and then set your mind to hearing what I have to say in all of this. Suppose a small child, of tender years, is brought to a teacher to be taught the Torah, which is a great good for him because of the perfection it will bring him; yet on account of his young age and the weakness of his understanding he does not grasp the measure of that good nor what perfection it leads him to. The teacher, who is more complete than he, is therefore obliged of necessity to spur him on to study by means of what he loves on account of his young age, and so says to him: "Read, and I will give you a walnut or a fig, or I will hand you a piece of sugar." So he reads and exerts himself — not for the reading itself, since he sets no value upon it, but to obtain that food; and eating that food is, in his eyes, better and more of a good than the reading, without any doubt. Therefore he reckons the reading a hardship and a toil that he undergoes in order, by that toil, to attain that beloved end, which is a nut or a piece of sugar.

So again he exerts himself — not for the reading itself, but for that clothing; for that garment is, in his eyes, better than learning, and is the end of his reading.

aligned.ja: פאד'א צאר אכמל עקל וצ'עף ענדה הד'א אלקדר איצ'א טמע במא הו אכת'ר מן הד'א, פיקול לה מעלמה אחפט' הד'ה אלפרשה או הד'א אלפרק ונדפע לך דינאר או דינארין, פיקרי איצ'א ויג'תהד ליאכ'ד' ד'לך אלמאל, ואכ'ד' אלמאל ענדה חיניד' אשרף מן אלקראה, לאן גאיהֵ אלקראה ענדה חיניד' אן יאכ'ד' אלד'הב אלד'י רג'י בה.
aligned.en: When he grows more perfect in mind and that too loses its worth for him, he sets his desire upon something higher than that, and his teacher says to him: "Learn this section, or this chapter, and I will give you a dinar or two." So he reads and exerts himself in order to take that money — and taking the money is then, in his eyes, more honorable than the reading, since the end of his reading is now that he should take the gold he was promised.

pairs.en: When he grows more perfect in mind
I will give you a dinar or two

pairs.ja: ואכ'ד' אלמאל ענדה חיניד' אשרף מן אלקראה
pairs.en: taking the money is then, in his eyes, more honorable than the reading

pairs.ja: גאיהֵ אלקראה ענדה חיניד' אן יאכ'ד' אלד'הב
pairs.en: the end of his reading is now that he should take the gold

aligned.ja: פאד'א צאר אכת'ר תמייז וצ'עף איצ'א ענדה הד'א אלקדר וראי אן ד'לך קדר כ'סיס טמע במא הו את'ר מן ד'לך, ויקאל לה אקרי לתציר רב ודיין יעט'מך אלנאס ויקפון אמאמך ויימתת'לון אואמרך ויעט'ם אסמך פי חיאתך ובעד ממאתך מת'ל פלאן ופלאן פיקרי ויג'תהד לינאל הד'ה אלרתבה, פתכון אלגאיה ענדה תעט'ים אלנאס ואג'לאלהם לה ות'נאהם עליה.
aligned.en: When he grows more discerning and this too loses its worth for him, seeing that it is a paltry thing, he sets his desire upon something greater still; and he is told: "Study, so that you may become a master and a judge, that people may honor you and rise before you and obey your commands, and that your name be magnified in your life and after your death, like so-and-so and so-and-so." So he reads and exerts himself to attain that rank, and his end is now that people should honor and exalt him and praise him.

pairs.en: you may become a master and a judge
people may honor you and rise before you

pairs.ja: ויעט'ם אסמך פי חיאתך ובעד ממאתך
pairs.en: your name be magnified in your life and after your death

pairs.ja: אלגאיה ענדה תעט'ים אלנאס ואג'לאלהם לה
pairs.en: his end is now that people should honor and exalt him

aligned.ja: והד'א כלה מד'מום, ואנמא ילתג'י לד'לך לצ'עף עקל אלשכ'ץ אלד'י יג'על גאיהֵ אלעלם שיא אכ'ר גיר אלעלם. פיקול לאי שי נעלם הד'א אלעלם אלא לננאל בה הדיאנהֵ עלי אלחקיקה, והד'א הו ענד אלחכמים שלא לשמה, אי אנה ימתת'ל אלשראיע ויעמלהא ויקרא ויג'תהד לא לד'לך אלשי פי נפסה בל לשי אכ'ר. ונהונא אלחכמים עליהם אלסלאם ען הד'א וקאלוא לא תעשם עטרה להתגדל בהם ולא קרדום לחפור בהם.
aligned.en: Now all of this is blameworthy. One resorts to it only because of the weakness of the person's mind, who makes the end of learning something other than learning itself, and says: "Why do we learn this knowledge, except to obtain by it these things?" — when [in truth] he should learn for the sake of [attaining] true wisdom. This is what the Sages call [learning] "not for its own sake" (*she-lo li-shmah*) — that is, that one fulfills the commandments, performs them, reads, and exerts himself, not for the sake of the thing itself but for the sake of some other thing. The Sages, may peace be upon them, forbade this and said: "Do not make them a crown to magnify yourself, nor a spade to dig with" (m. Avot 4:5).

pairs.en: all of this is blameworthy

pairs.ja: יג'על גאיהֵ אלעלם שיא אכ'ר גיר אלעלם
pairs.en: makes the end of learning something other than learning itself
"not for its own sake" (*she-lo li-shmah*)

pairs.ja: לא לד'לך אלשי פי נפסה בל לשי אכ'ר
pairs.en: not for the sake of the thing itself but for the sake of some other thing

pairs.ja: לא תעשם עטרה להתגדל בהם ולא קרדום לחפור בהם
pairs.en: "Do not make them a crown to magnify yourself, nor a spade to dig with"

aligned.ja: ישירון אלי מא בינת לך אנה לא יג'על גאיהֵ אלעלם לא תעט'ים אלנאס לה ולא אכתסאב אלמאל, ולא יתכ'ד' דין אללה מעישה, ולא תכון ענדה גאיהֵ אלעלם אלא עלמה פקט. וכד'לך ליס גאיהֵ אלחק אלא אן יעלם אנה חק, ואלשראיע חק פגאיתהא אמתת'להא.
aligned.en: — alluding to what I have explained to you, that one should not make the end of knowledge the people's honoring of him, nor the acquiring of money, and should not take the religion of God as a livelihood, but should have no end in his learning other than the knowledge itself. So too, the end of [grasping] the truth is only to know that it is true; and the [revealed] laws are true, so their end is the fulfilling of them.

pairs.ja: לא תעט'ים אלנאס לה ולא אכתסאב אלמאל
pairs.en: not make the end of knowledge the people's honoring of him, nor the acquiring of money
should not take the religion of God as a livelihood
no end in his learning other than the knowledge itself
the [revealed] laws are true, so their end is the fulfilling of them

aligned.ja: ולא יג'וז לאלאנסאן אלכאמל אן יקול אן עמלת הד'ה אלפצ'איל ואג'תנבת הד'ה אלקבאיח אלתי נהי אללה ענהא באי שי נג'אזא, לאן ד'לך מת'ל קול אלצבי אד'א קרית אי שי ידפע לי פיקאל לה אלאמר אלפלאני, לאנא אד'א ראינא צ'עף עקלה אלד'י לם יפהם הד'א אלקדר וטלב לאלגאיה גאיה נג'אובה עלי קדר ג'הלה ענה כסיל כאולתו.
aligned.en: A complete person ought not to say, "If I practice these virtues and shun these vices which God forbade, with what shall I be rewarded?" — for that is like the saying of the child: "If I read, what will be given me?" — to which the answer is, "Such-and-such a thing." For when we see the weakness of his mind, which cannot grasp this much and seeks an end for the end, we answer him according to his ignorance, [as it is written,] "Answer a fool according to his folly" (Proverbs 26:5).

pairs.en: A complete person

pairs.ja: עמלת הד'ה אלפצ'איל ואג'תנבת הד'ה אלקבאיח
pairs.en: I practice these virtues and shun these vices
with what shall I be rewarded

pairs.ja: נג'אובה עלי קדר ג'הלה ענה כסיל כאולתו
pairs.en: we answer him according to his ignorance, [as it is written,] "Answer a fool according to his folly"

aligned.ja: וקד נהונא אלחכמים ען הד'א איצ'א אעני אן יג'על אלאנסאן גאיהֵ עבאדתה ואמתת'אלה לאלשראיע אמר מן אלאמור, והו קול אלפאצ'ל אלכאמל אלמדרך אלחקאיק אנטגנס איש שוכו אל תהיו כעבדים המשמשין את הרב על מנת לקבל פרס אלא היו כעבדים המשמשין את הרב על מנת שלא לקבל פרס, ואנמא אראדוא בד'לך אן יעתקד אלחק לנפס אלחק, והד'א הו אלמעני אלד'י יעברון ענה בעובד מאהבה.
aligned.en: The Sages have forbidden us this too — namely, that a person should make some [external] thing the end of his worship and of his fulfilling the commandments. This is the saying of the perfect, complete man who apprehends the truths, Antigonos of Sokho: "Be not like servants who serve the master in order to receive a reward, but be like servants who serve the master not in order to receive a reward" (m. Avot 1:3). By this they meant that one should believe the truth for the sake of the truth itself; and this is the meaning they express by [the phrase] "one who worships out of love."

pairs.en: the perfect, complete man who apprehends the truths
Antigonos of Sokho

pairs.ja: אל תהיו כעבדים המשמשין את הרב על מנת לקבל פרס
pairs.en: "Be not like servants who serve the master in order to receive a reward, but be like servants who serve the master not in order to receive a reward"
one should believe the truth for the sake of the truth itself
"one who worships out of love."

aligned.ja: וקאלוא עליהם אלסלאם במצותיו חפץ מאד אמר ר' אלעזר במצותיו ולא בשכר מצותיו, ומא אעט'ם הד'א אלדליל ומא אבינה פאנה דליל ואצ'ח עלי מא תקדם לנא מן אלקול.
aligned.en: The Sages, may peace be upon them, said concerning the verse "He delights greatly in His commandments" (Psalms 112:1): "R. Eliezer said: 'in His commandments' — and not in the reward of His commandments" (BT Avodah Zarah 19a). How great is this proof and how clear! For it is a plain demonstration of what we said before.

pairs.en: "He delights greatly in His commandments"
'in His commandments' — and not in the reward of His commandments
this proof

aligned.ja: ואעט'ם מן הד'א קולהם פי נץ ספרי שמא תאמר הריני למד תורה בשביל שאהיה עשיר בשביל שאקרא רבי בשביל שאקבל שכר בעולם הבא תלמוד לומר לאהבה את ה' כל שאתם עושים לא תעשו אלא מאהבה.
aligned.en: And greater still than this is their saying in the text of the *Sifrei*: "Lest you say, 'Behold, I will study Torah in order to be rich, in order to be called Rabbi, in order to receive reward in the World to Come' — Scripture teaches, 'to love the Lord' (Deuteronomy 11:13): whatever you do, do only out of love" (Sifrei Deuteronomy 41).

pairs.en: in the text of the *Sifrei*

pairs.ja: הריני למד תורה בשביל שאהיה עשיר
pairs.en: 'Behold, I will study Torah in order to be rich, in order to be called Rabbi, in order to receive reward in the World to Come'
in order to be called Rabbi

pairs.ja: כל שאתם עושים לא תעשו אלא מאהבה
pairs.en: whatever you do, do only out of love

aligned.ja: פקד תבין הד'א אלמעני וצח אנה ג'רץ אלשרע וקאעדהֵ אעתקאד אלחכמים, ולא יתעאמי ענה אלא ג'אהל גבי קד אתלפתה וסוסה אלאפכאר אלסכ'יפה ואלתכ'ילאת אלנאקצה, והד'ה הי דרג'הֵ אברהם אבינו אנה כאן עובד מאהבה, ונחו הד'א אלטריק ילזם אלנזוע.
aligned.en: So this meaning has become clear, and it is established that this is the aim of the [revealed] Law and the foundation of the belief of the Sages. None turns a blind eye to it save an ignorant fool whom the whisperings of feeble notions and defective fancies have ruined. This is the rank of Abraham our father, who worshiped out of love; and it is along this path that one is bound to strive.

pairs.en: the aim of the [revealed] Law and the foundation of the belief of the Sages
the whisperings of feeble notions and defective fancies

pairs.ja: דרג'הֵ אברהם אבינו אנה כאן עובד מאהבה
pairs.en: the rank of Abraham our father, who worshiped out of love
it is along this path that one is bound to strive

aligned.ja: ולעלם אלחכמים עליהם אלסלאם אן הד'א אלמעני עויץ ג'דא ומא כל אחד ידרכה, ואן אדרכה פליס יואפקה מן אול מרה ולא יראה אעתקאדא צחיח, לאן אלאנסאן לא יפעל אפעאל אלא לינאל בהא נפע או ידפע מצ'רה, או יכון פעלה ד'לך עבת', פכיף יקאל לאלמתשרע אפעל הד'ה אלאפעאל ולא תפעלהא לא לכ'וף מן עקאב אללה ולא לתרג'י ת'ואבה, הד'א צעב ג'דא, לאן ליס כל אלנאס ידרכון אלחקאיק ויכונון מת'ל אברהם אבינו.
aligned.en: Yet because the Sages, may peace be upon them, knew that this matter is exceedingly hard, and not everyone apprehends it, and even one who does apprehend it does not at first accept it nor regard it as a sound belief — for a person performs his deeds only to attain some benefit or ward off some harm, else his action is in vain; so how can one say to a person bound by the Law, "Perform these deeds, but do not perform them out of fear of God's punishment or in hope of His reward"? This is very hard, since not all people apprehend the truths and become like Abraham our father.

pairs.en: this matter is exceedingly hard

pairs.ja: אלאנסאן לא יפעל אפעאל אלא לינאל בהא נפע או ידפע מצ'רה
pairs.en: a person performs his deeds only to attain some benefit or ward off some harm

pairs.ja: לא לכ'וף מן עקאב אללה ולא לתרג'י ת'ואבה
pairs.en: not perform them out of fear of God's punishment or in hope of His reward
not all people apprehend the truths

aligned.ja: פאבאחוא לאלג'מהור אן יקרוא עלי אעתקאדהם מן פעל אלחסנאת לתרג'י אלת'ואב, ואג'תנאב אלסיאת כ'וף אלעקאב, ויחצ'ון עלי ד'לך ותקוי עזאימהם פיה, חתי ידרך אלמדרך פיערף אלחק ואלוג'ה אלאכמל מא הו, כמת'ל מא נפעל באלצבי ענד אלתעלים עלי מא מת'לנא.
aligned.en: — they therefore permitted the multitude to remain in their belief that they do good deeds in hope of reward and shun evil deeds in fear of punishment, and they urge them on in this and strengthen their resolve in it, until the one capable of apprehending apprehends and comes to know the truth and the most perfect way. This is just as we deal with the child in teaching him, as in the parable we set out.

pairs.en: they therefore permitted the multitude
they do good deeds in hope of reward
shun evil deeds in fear of punishment

pairs.ja: חתי ידרך אלמדרך פיערף אלחק ואלוג'ה אלאכמל
pairs.en: until the one capable of apprehending apprehends and comes to know the truth and the most perfect way

aligned.ja: ונקדוא עלי אנטגנס איש סוכו פי תצריחה פי אלג'מהור במא צרח, וקאלוא פי ד'לך חכמים הזהרו בדבריכם וכו' עלי מא סנבין פי אבות, ולא הם אלג'מהור כ'אסרון מרה ואחדה פי כונהם ימתת'לון אלשריעה לכ'וף עקאב ותרג'י אלת'ואב לכנהם גיר כאמלין, ואנמא יסתחב להם ד'לך לתחצל להם מלכה וריאצ'ה פי אמתת'אל אלשריעה וינתקלון אלי אלחק ויצירון עובדים מאהבה, והו קולהם עליהם אלסלאם לעולם יעסוק אדם בתורה אפילו שלא לשמה שמתוך שלא לשמה בא לשמה.
aligned.en: And they faulted Antigonos of Sokho for declaring openly to the multitude what he declared, and said concerning this: "Sages, be careful with your words" etc. (m. Avot 1:11), as we shall explain in [our commentary on] Avot. The multitude lose nothing thereby; for in their fulfilling the Law out of fear of punishment and hope of reward, [it is true] they are not complete — but this is to be encouraged in them, so that they may acquire a settled disposition and a habit in fulfilling the Law, and may pass on to the truth and become "those who worship out of love." This is their saying, may peace be upon them: "Let a person always occupy himself with the Torah even not for its own sake, for from [doing it] not for its own sake he comes to [doing it] for its own sake" (BT Pesaḥim 50b).

pairs.ja: נקדוא עלי אנטגנס איש סוכו פי תצריחה פי אלג'מהור
pairs.en: they faulted Antigonos of Sokho for declaring openly to the multitude
"Sages, be careful with your words"
a settled disposition and a habit in fulfilling the Law
"those who worship out of love."

pairs.ja: לעולם יעסוק אדם בתורה אפילו שלא לשמה שמתוך שלא לשמה בא לשמה
pairs.en: "Let a person always occupy himself with the Torah even not for its own sake, for from [doing it] not for its own sake he comes to [doing it] for its own sake"

aligned.ja: וממא יג'ב אן תעלמה אן כלאם אלחכמים עליהם אלסלאם אנקסמוא אלנאס פיה ת'לאת' פרק.
aligned.en: Now among the things you must know is that, with respect to the sayings of the Sages, may peace be upon them, people have divided into three groups.

pairs.en: the sayings of the Sages, may peace be upon them
people have divided into three groups

aligned.ja: אלפרקה אלאולי והי אכת'ר מן ראיתה ומן ראית תואליפה ומן סמעת בה, תחמלה עלי ט'אהרה ולא תתאולה בוג'ה, ותציר ענדהא אלממתנעאת כלהא ואג'בהֵ אלוג'וד, ואנמא פעלוא ד'לך לג'הלהם באלעלום ובעדהם מן אלמעארף, וליס הם מן אלכמאל מן חית' ינתבהון מן תלקי אנפסהם ולא וג'דוא מנבהא ינבההם פהם ירון אן לם ירידוא אלחכמים בג'מיע אקואלהם אלמחכמה אלא מא פהמוא הם מנהא ואנהא עלי ט'ואהרהא.
aligned.en: [The First Approach — the Crude Literalists.] The first group — and they are the majority of those I have seen, and of those whose compositions I have seen and of whom I have heard — take [the Sages' words] according to their plain sense and do not interpret them figuratively at all; to them all the impossibilities become necessities of existence. They did this only out of their ignorance of the sciences and their remoteness from the branches of knowledge, and because they are not perfect enough to rouse themselves of their own accord, nor have they found anyone to rouse them. So they suppose that the Sages, in all their well-considered sayings, intended nothing but what they themselves understood from them and that [these sayings are] to be taken at face value.

pairs.en: The first group

pairs.ja: תחמלה עלי ט'אהרה ולא תתאולה בוג'ה
pairs.en: take [the Sages' words] according to their plain sense and do not interpret them figuratively at all
all the impossibilities become necessities of existence
out of their ignorance of the sciences and their remoteness from the branches of knowledge

pairs.ja: לם ירידוא אלחכמים בג'מיע אקואלהם אלמחכמה אלא מא פהמוא הם מנהא
pairs.en: the Sages, in all their well-considered sayings, intended nothing but what they themselves understood from them

aligned.ja: ואן כאנת ט'ואהר בעץ' כלאמהם מן אלשנאעה פי חיז לו וצף עלי ט'אהרה לעואם אלנאס נאהיך ען כ'ואצהם לאבהתוא אעתבארא וקאלוא כיף יכון פי אלדניא שכ'ץ יתכ'יל הד'א ויראה ראיא צחיחא נאהיך ען אסתחסאנה. והד'ה אלטאיפה אלמסכינה ירת'י לג'הלהא לאנהא עט'מת אלחכמים בזעמהא והי קד אחטתהם גאיהֵ אלחטאט והי לא תשער.
aligned.en: — even though the plain sense of some of their words is of a strangeness such that, were it described to the common people at its face value (let alone to the elite), they would be astonished and say, "How could there be in the world anyone who imagines this and regards it as a sound view, let alone deems it good?" This wretched group is to be pitied for its ignorance: for it has, by its own reckoning, exalted the Sages, when in truth it has degraded them to the utmost degree of degradation without realizing it.

pairs.en: the plain sense of some of their words is of a strangeness
the common people at its face value (let alone to the elite)
This wretched group

pairs.ja: עט'מת אלחכמים בזעמהא והי קד אחטתהם גאיהֵ אלחטאט
pairs.en: it has, by its own reckoning, exalted the Sages, when in truth it has degraded them to the utmost degree of degradation

aligned.ja: ואן כאן לעמר אללה הד'ה אלטאיפה תד'הב במחאסן אלדין ותט'לם בהג'תה ותג'על דין אללה פי עכס מא אריד בה, לאן אללה יקול פי מחכם אלתנזיל אשר ישמעון את כל החקים האלה וכו' והד'ה אלטאיפה תסרד מן ט'ואהר כלאם אלחכמים מא אד'א סמעתה אלמלל קאלוא רק עם סכל ונבל הגוי הקטן הזה.
aligned.en: By the life of God, this group does away with the beauty of the religion, darkens its splendor, and turns the religion of God into the very opposite of what was intended by it. For God says in the perfect text of the revelation, "[the nations] who shall hear all these statutes [and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people]" (Deuteronomy 4:6) — yet this group recites, from the plain sense of the Sages' words, things that, when the nations hear them, lead them to say, "Surely this little nation is a foolish and senseless people."

pairs.en: does away with the beauty of the religion, darkens its splendor

pairs.ja: תג'על דין אללה פי עכס מא אריד בה
pairs.en: turns the religion of God into the very opposite of what was intended by it

pairs.ja: אשר ישמעון את כל החקים האלה
pairs.en: "[the nations] who shall hear all these statutes [and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people]"

pairs.ja: רק עם סכל ונבל הגוי הקטן הזה
pairs.en: "Surely this little nation is a foolish and senseless people."

aligned.ja: ואכת'ר מן יפעל הד'א אלדרשנין אלד'ין יפהמון אלנאס מא לם יפהמוה הם, פיא ליתהם אד' לא יפהמוא לו סכתוא מי יתן החרש תחרישון ותהי לכם לחכמה, או כאן יקולון מא נעלם מא אראד אלחכמים בהד'א אלכלאם ולא כיף יתאול, בל יזעמון פהמה ויג'עלון אידיהם פי תפהים אלנאס מא פהמוא הם באנפסהם לא מא קאל אלחכמים, ויעלנון עלי ראווס אלג'מהור בדרשות ברכות ופרק חלק וגירהמא עלי ט'ואהרהא חרפא בחרף.
aligned.en: Those who do this most are the preachers (*darshanim*) who explain to the people what they themselves have not understood. Would that, since they understood nothing, they had at least kept silent — "If only you would keep utterly silent, that would be wisdom for you" (Job 13:5) — or that they had said, "We do not know what the Sages meant by these words, nor how they are to be interpreted." But they suppose they understand, and set themselves to teaching the people what they themselves understood — not what the Sages [meant] — and they expound to the masses the homilies of [tractate] Berakhot and of the chapter *Ḥeleq* and the like at their plain sense, word for word.

pairs.ja: אלדרשנין אלד'ין יפהמון אלנאס מא לם יפהמוה הם
pairs.en: the preachers (*darshanim*) who explain to the people what they themselves have not understood

pairs.ja: מי יתן החרש תחרישון ותהי לכם לחכמה
pairs.en: "If only you would keep utterly silent, that would be wisdom for you"
the homilies of [tractate] Berakhot and of the chapter *Ḥeleq*

aligned.ja: ואלטאיפה אלת'אניה כת'ירה איצ'א והם אלד'ין ראוא כלאם אלחכמים או סמעוה פחמלוה עלי ט'אהרה וזעמוא אן מא אראדוא אלחכמים בד'לך גיר מא דל עליה ט'אהר אלכלאם, פאקבלוא עלי תסכ'יפה ותקביחה ותשניע מא ליס בשניע, וילעיגו על דברי חכמים מע אלאחיאן, ויזעמון אנהם אעקל מנהם ואד'כי ד'הן, ואנהם עליהם אלסלאם מנכ'דעין נאקצי אלראי ג'אהלין בג'מלה אלוג'וד לא ידרכוא שי בוג'ה.
aligned.en: [The Second Approach — the Embarrassed Allegorizers.] The second group is also numerous: these are those who saw or heard the sayings of the Sages, took them at their plain sense, and supposed that the Sages meant nothing by them but what the plain sense of the words indicates; and so they set themselves to belittling and disparaging them, and to denouncing as outrageous what is not outrageous, and at times they mock the words of the Sages, and suppose themselves more intelligent and of keener mind, and [suppose] that the Sages, may peace be upon them, were deluded, deficient in judgment, and ignorant of the whole of existence, apprehending nothing at all.

pairs.en: The second group

pairs.en: took them at their plain sense, and supposed that the Sages meant nothing by them but what the plain sense of the words indicates
they mock the words of the Sages

pairs.ja: מנכ'דעין נאקצי אלראי ג'אהלין בג'מלה אלוג'וד
pairs.en: deluded, deficient in judgment, and ignorant of the whole of existence

aligned.ja: ואכת'ר מא יקע פי הד'א אלאעתקאד מדעיי אלטב, ואלהד'איין בקצ'איא אלנג'ום, לאנהם בזעמהם חד'אק חכמא פלאספה, ומא אבעדהם מן אלאנסאניה ענד אלפלאספה עלי אלחקיקה, והם אג'הל מן אלפרקה אלאולי ואכת'ר גבאוה, והי טאיפה מלעונה לתהאפתהא לאשכ'אץ עט'מא אלקדר קד באן עלמהם ענד אלעלמא.
aligned.en: Most who fall into this belief are pretenders to medicine and those who rave with the verdicts of astrology, since they fancy themselves clever, wise philosophers — though how far they are, in truth, from being human beings in the eyes of [genuine] philosophers! They are more ignorant than the first group and more foolish; and it is an accursed faction, for it presumes against persons of high rank whose learning has been made plain to the learned.

pairs.en: pretenders to medicine and those who rave with the verdicts of astrology
they fancy themselves clever, wise philosophers

pairs.ja: אג'הל מן אלפרקה אלאולי ואכת'ר גבאוה
pairs.en: more ignorant than the first group and more foolish
an accursed faction

aligned.ja: ולו אנהם ראצ'וא אנפסהם פי אלעלום חתי יעלמון כיף ינבגי אן יוקע אלכלאם פי אלאלאהיאת ושבההא מן אלאמור ענד אלג'מהור וענד אלכ'ואץ, ויחכמון אלג'ז אלעמלי מן אלפלספה לבאן להם הל אלחכמים עלמא או לא, וכאן ינפהם להם מעאני כלאמהם.
aligned.en: Had they but trained themselves in the sciences, so as to know how discourse upon divine matters and the like ought to be conducted before the multitude and before the elite, and had they mastered the practical part of philosophy, it would have become plain to them whether the Sages were learned or not, and the meanings of their words would have become clear to them.

pairs.ja: כיף ינבגי אן יוקע אלכלאם פי אלאלאהיאת
pairs.en: how discourse upon divine matters and the like ought to be conducted before the multitude
before the multitude and before the elite
the practical part of philosophy
the meanings of their words

aligned.ja: ואלטאיפה אלת'אלתה והי לעמר אללה קלילה ג'דא חתי לא יקאל להא טאיפה אלא כמא יקאל לאלשמס נוע, והם אלאקואם אלד'ין תקרר ענדהם עט'ם אלחכמים וג'ודהֵ אפכארהם במא וג'ד פי טי כלאמהם כלמאת תדל עלי מעאני צחיחה ג'דא, ואן כאנת קלילה ומפתרקה פי מואצ'ע מן מדונאתהם, לכנהא דלת עלי כמאלהם ואדראכהם אלחקאיק.
aligned.en: [Rambam's Approach.] The third group — and by the life of God they are exceedingly few, so few that they can scarcely be called a "group" except as one calls the sun a "species" — are those for whom the greatness of the Sages and the excellence of their thought have been established by what is found woven into their words, [namely] phrases that point to entirely sound meanings, even if these are few and scattered in [various] places of their compilations; yet they prove [the Sages'] perfection and their apprehension of the truths.

pairs.en: The third group

pairs.ja: קלילה ג'דא חתי לא יקאל להא טאיפה אלא כמא יקאל לאלשמס נוע
pairs.en: so few that they can scarcely be called a "group" except as one calls the sun a "species"
the greatness of the Sages and the excellence of their thought

pairs.ja: כלמאת תדל עלי מעאני צחיחה ג'דא
pairs.en: phrases that point to entirely sound meanings
their apprehension of the truths

aligned.ja: ותקרר איצ'א ענדהם אמתנאע אלממתנע ווג'וב אלואג'ב, פעלמוא אנהם עליהם אלסלאם לא יתכלמון פי מחאל, פתיקנוא אן כלאמהם לה ט'אהר ובאטן, ואנה כל מא יקולון מן אלאשיא אלגיר ממכנה אנמא כלאמהם פיהא עלי סביל אללגז ואלמת'ל, והכד'א שאן אלחכמא אלכבאר.
aligned.en: There has also been established for them the impossibility of the impossible and the necessity of the necessary, so that they know that the Sages, may peace be upon them, do not speak of what is absurd; and they are convinced that [the Sages'] words have an outer sense and an inner sense, and that whatever [the Sages] say of impossible things, their discourse upon them is by way of riddle and parable. Such is the way of the great sages.

pairs.en: the impossibility of the impossible and the necessity of the necessary
do not speak of what is absurd
[the Sages'] words have an outer sense and an inner sense
by way of riddle and parable

aligned.ja: ולהד'א צדר כתאבה רייס אלחכמא וקאל להבין משל ומליצה דברי חכמים וחידותם, וקד עלם מן ערף אללגה אן חידה הו אלכלאם אלד'י גרצ'ה פי באטנה לא פי ט'אהרה וכמא קאל אחודה נא לכם חידה וכו', לאן כלאם אהל אלעלם כלהם פי אלאמור אלרפיעה אלתי הי אלגאיה אנמא הו לגז ומת'ל.
aligned.en: Therefore the chief of the sages [Solomon] opened his book and said: "To understand a parable and a metaphor, the words of the wise and their riddles" (Proverbs 1:6). And whoever knows the [Hebrew] language knows that *ḥidah* (riddle) is discourse whose aim lies in its inner, not its outer, sense, as in "Let me put a riddle to you" (Judges 14:12). For the discourse of all the men of knowledge upon those sublime matters which are the [ultimate] end is by way of riddle and parable.

pairs.en: the chief of the sages [Solomon]

pairs.ja: להבין משל ומליצה דברי חכמים וחידותם
pairs.en: "To understand a parable and a metaphor, the words of the wise and their riddles"

pairs.ja: חידה הו אלכלאם אלד'י גרצ'ה פי באטנה לא פי ט'אהרה
pairs.en: *ḥidah* (riddle) is discourse whose aim lies in its inner, not its outer, sense
those sublime matters which are the [ultimate] end

aligned.ja: וכיף יסתנכר יא קום תאליפהם אלעלם עלי טריק אלמת'ל ואלתשביה באמור כ'סיסה עאמיה ותרי אחכם אלנאס קד פעל ד'לך ברוח הקדש אעני שלמה פי משלי ושיר השירים ובעץ' קהלת.
aligned.en: How, O people, can you find it strange that they composed [their] knowledge by way of parable, likening it to base and common things, when you see the wisest of men do this by the holy spirit — I mean Solomon — in Proverbs, the Song of Songs, and part of Ecclesiastes?

pairs.ja: תאליפהם אלעלם עלי טריק אלמת'ל ואלתשביה
pairs.en: they composed [their] knowledge by way of parable, likening it

pairs.ja: אחכם אלנאס קד פעל ד'לך ברוח הקדש
pairs.en: the wisest of men do this by the holy spirit

pairs.ja: שלמה פי משלי ושיר השירים ובעץ' קהלת
pairs.en: Solomon — in Proverbs, the Song of Songs, and part of Ecclesiastes

aligned.ja: וכיף יסתנכר תאויל כלאמהם ואכ'ראג'ה ען ט'אהרה חתי יטאבק אלעקל ויואפק אלחק וכתב אלתנזיל, והם באנפסהם יתאולון נצוץ אלכתב ויכ'רג'ונהא ען ט'אהרהא ויג'עלונהא מת'ל והו אלחק, כמא נג'דהם יקולון אן קול אלכתאב הוא הכה את שני אריאל מואב כלה מת'ל, וכד'לך קולה הוא הכה את הארי בתוך הבור וכו' מת'ל, וקולה מי ישקני
aligned.en:
And how can you find it strange to interpret their words and draw them out from their plain sense so that they accord with reason and agree with the truth and with the books of revelation, when [the Sages] themselves interpret the verses of Scripture, drawing them out from their plain sense and rendering them parable — and this is the truth? For we find them saying that the verse "He smote two ariels of Moab" (2 Samuel 23:20) is a parable; and likewise "he went down and slew the lion in the midst of the pit" (2 Samuel 23:20) is a parable; and "who will give me water to drink" (2 Samuel 23:15) and the rest of what occurs there — all of it is parable. So too the book of Job in its entirety: some of them said it was a parable, but did not make plain to what end the parable was set. So too the vision of Ezekiel: some of them said it was a parable. And much of this kind.

So if you, sir, are of either of the first two groups, pay no heed to my words on any of this matter, for nothing of it will agree with you; rather it will harm you and you will hate it. How should light, temperate food, of measured quantity and balanced quality, suit a person who has grown accustomed to bad, heavy foods? It would actually injure him and he would loathe it. Do you not see what those who were accustomed to eating onions and garlic and fish said of the manna? — "and our soul loathes this insubstantial bread" (Numbers 21:5). But if you are of the third group, then whenever there comes before you any of their words that reason rejects, pause at it and know that it is a riddle and a parable; and lie down with mind absorbed and thought given over to interpreting it, intent upon attaining the doctrine of truth and the right view, as it is said: "to find delightful words and to write rightly words of truth" (Ecclesiastes 12:10). Consider my words, and you will succeed, if God, exalted be He, so wills.

pairs.en: interpret their words and draw them out from their plain sense so that they accord with reason and agree with the truth

pairs.ja: הוא הכה את שני אריאל מואב כלה מת'ל
pairs.en: the verse "He smote two ariels of Moab" (2 Samuel 23:20) is a parable

A human being should not be so; rather what restrains him should be his very self — I mean his human form, which, when it is complete, restrains him from those things that the [state of] completeness restrains [him from], and these are called the vices, and it urges him on toward that by which he is made complete, and these are the virtues. This is what I have been able to gather from the whole of their words upon this sublime and momentous matter.

I shall [one day] compose a work in which I gather all the homilies (*derashot*) found in the Talmud and elsewhere, and explain them, and interpret them in a way that accords with the truths, adducing proof for all of this from [the Sages'] own words; I shall show which of them are at their plain sense, which are parable, and which befell in dream and were recorded in unqualified terms as though they had befallen while awake. In that work I shall make plain to you many beliefs; and in it I shall set out the full account of those matters of which I have here given you only a few small samples by which to measure the rest. Rather it is toward Him, may He be exalted, that one's thoughts should aim, setting aside all that is below Him. This fifth principle is the prohibition of idolatry, and most of the Torah is [taken up] with prohibiting it.

aligned.ja: ואלפצל אלת'אני אן כל נבי לא יאתיה אלוחי אלא פי חאל אלנום כמא קאל פי מואצ'ע בחלום הלילה, ויחלום, בחלום חזיון לילה וכו', וכת'יר מן הד'א אלגרץ'. או באלנהאר בעד סבאת יציב אלנבי וחאלה תתעטל פיהא חואסה ותכ'לי פכרתה שבה נום, והד'ה אלחאלה תתסמי מחזה ומראה, וענהא יקול במראות אלהים, ומשה יאתיה אלכ'טאב באלנהאר והוא עומד בין שני הכרובים כמא ועדה אללה ונועדתי לך שם ודברתי אתך וכו', קאל תעלי אם יהיה נביאכם ה' במראה אליו אתודע בחלום אדבר בו לא כן עבדי משה.
aligned.en: The second distinction: to every [other] prophet revelation comes only in a state of sleep, as it says in [various] places, "in a dream of the night," "and he dreamed," "in a dream, a vision of the night," and much of this purport — or by day, after a deep sleep falls upon the prophet and a state overtakes him in which his senses are suspended and his thought left empty, like sleep; and this state is called *maḥazeh* and *marʾeh*, and it is of this that [Scripture] says "in visions of God" (Ezekiel 1:1). But to Moses the address came by day, "as he stood between the two cherubim," as God promised him, "and I will meet with you there and speak with you" etc. (Exodus 25:22). [God], may He be exalted, said: "If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord make Myself known to him in a vision, in a dream I speak with him; not so My servant Moses" (Numbers 12:6–7).

pairs.en: The second distinction

pairs.ja: לא יאתיה אלוחי אלא פי חאל אלנום
pairs.en: revelation comes only in a state of sleep
in a dream of the night
*maḥazeh* and *marʾeh*
as he stood between the two cherubim
not so My servant Moses

aligned.ja: ואלפצל אלת'אלת' אן אלנבי אד'א אתאה אלוחי ועלי אנה במראה ועל ידי מלאך תכ'ור טבאעה ותכ'תל בניתה וירד עליה הול עט'ים ג'דא יכאד ינפטר מנה כמא בין פי דניאל פי כלאם גבריאל לה במראה קאל ולא נשאר בי כח והודי נהפך עלי למשחית ולא עצרתי כח, וקאל ואני הייתי נרדם על פני ופני ארצה, וקאל במראה נהפכו צירי עלי.
aligned.en: The third distinction: when revelation comes to a [other] prophet — even in a vision and by means of an angel — his nature flags, his frame is shaken, and an exceedingly great terror falls upon him so that he is all but undone, as is made plain concerning Daniel: in Gabriel's speaking to him in a vision he said, "and no strength remained in me, and my comeliness was turned in me to corruption, and I retained no strength" (Daniel 10:8), and "but I had been in a deep sleep upon my face, with my face to the ground" (Daniel 10:9), and "in the vision my pangs were turned upon me" (Daniel 10:16).

pairs.en: The third distinction
his nature flags, his frame is shaken

pairs.ja: הול עט'ים ג'דא יכאד ינפטר מנה
pairs.en: an exceedingly great terror falls upon him so that he is all but undone
no strength remained in me
in a deep sleep upon my face, with my face to the ground

aligned.ja: ומשה ליס כד'לך בל יאתיה אלכ'טאב פלא ילחקה אצ'טראב בוג'ה והו קולה ודבר ה' אל משה פנים אל פנים כאשר ידבר איש אל רעהו, יעני כמא לא יציב אלאנסאן אנזעאג' מן כלאם צאחבה כד'לך הו עליה אלסלאם מא כאן ינזעג' מן אלכ'טאב ואן כאן פנים בפנים, והד'א לשדהֵ אתצאלה באלעקל כמא קלנא.
aligned.en: But Moses is not so; rather the address comes to him without any disturbance at all overtaking him — this is the saying, "And the Lord spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his fellow" (Exodus 33:11), meaning that just as a man is not seized with alarm at the speech of his fellow, so too he, may peace be upon him, was not alarmed by the address, even though it was "face to face" — and this is by reason of the strength of his conjunction with the intellect, as we said.

pairs.en: without any disturbance at all overtaking him

pairs.ja: ודבר ה' אל משה פנים אל פנים
pairs.en: And the Lord spoke to Moses face to face

pairs.ja: כמא לא יציב אלאנסאן אנזעאג' מן כלאם צאחבה
pairs.en: just as a man is not seized with alarm at the speech of his fellow
the strength of his conjunction with the intellect

aligned.ja: ואלפצל אלראבע אן ג'מיע אלאנביא ליס יאתיהם אלוחי באכ'תיארהם בל באראדהֵ אללה, פקד יבקי אלנבי מדהֵ סנין לא יאתיה וחי, וקד יטלב מן אלנבי אן יכ'בר בוחי פיבקי חתי ינבי בה בעד איאם או בעד אשהר או לא יעלם בה בוג'ה.
aligned.en: The fourth distinction: to all the [other] prophets revelation does not come at their own choosing but by the will of God; for a prophet may remain for years without revelation coming to him, and a prophet may be asked to deliver some [matter] by revelation and may [have to] wait until he prophesies it after days, or after months, or may never come to know it at all.

pairs.en: The fourth distinction

pairs.ja: ליס יאתיהם אלוחי באכ'תיארהם בל באראדהֵ אללה
pairs.en: revelation does not come at their own choosing but by the will of God

pairs.ja: יבקי אלנבי מדהֵ סנין לא יאתיה וחי
pairs.en: a prophet may remain for years without revelation coming to him

aligned.ja: וקד ראינא מנהם מן יתהיי באן יבסט נפסה ויצפי כ'אטרה כמא פעל אלישע פי קולה קחו לי מנגן פג'אוה אלוחי, וליס הו צ'רורי אן יוחי אליה מתי תהייא, ומשה רבינו מתי שא קאל עמדו ואשמעה מה יצוה ה' לכם, וקאל דבר אל אהרן אחיך ואל יבוא בכל עת וקאלוא אהרן בבל יבוא ואין משה בבל יבוא.
aligned.en: We have [also] seen among them one who would prepare himself, putting his soul at ease and clearing his mind, as Elisha did when he said, "bring me a musician" (2 Kings 3:15), whereupon revelation came to him — yet it was not necessary that revelation come to him whenever he prepared himself. But Moses our Teacher, whenever he wished, would say, "Wait, and I will hear what the Lord commands concerning you" (Numbers 9:8), and "Speak to Aaron your brother, that he come not at all times [into the holy place]" (Leviticus 16:2); and [the Sages] said: "Aaron was under [the rule of] 'let him not come,' but Moses was not under 'let him not come'" (Sifra, Aḥarei Mot).

pairs.en: putting his soul at ease and clearing his mind
bring me a musician
Moses our Teacher, whenever he wished

pairs.ja: עמדו ואשמעה מה יצוה ה' לכם
pairs.en: Wait, and I will hear what the Lord commands concerning you

pairs.ja: אהרן בבל יבוא ואין משה בבל יבוא
pairs.en: Aaron was under [the rule of] 'let him not come,' but Moses was not under 'let him not come'

aligned.ja: ואלקאעדה אלת'אמנה הי תורה מן השמים. וד'לך באן יעתקד אן ג'מיע הד'ה אלתורה אלמוג'ודה באידינא יומנא הד'א הי אלתורה אלמנזלה עלי משה, ואנהא כלהא מפי הגבורה אעני אנהא וצלח לה כלהא מן קבל אללה אלוצול אלד'י יסמיה עלי סביל אלמג'אז כלאם, ולא יעלם כיפיהֵ ד'לך אלוצול אלא הו עליה אלסלאם, אלד'י וצל אליה, ואנה במנזלה נאסך' ימלי עליה והו ינסך' ויכתב ג'מיעהא תוארכ'הא ואכ'בארהא ושראיעהא וכד'א סמי מחוקק.
aligned.en: **The Eighth Principle** — that the Torah is from Heaven. That is, that one should believe that this entire Torah, which is in our hands today, is the Torah sent down upon Moses, and that all of it is "from the mouth of the Almighty" — meaning that it reached him, all of it, from God by that reaching which is called, figuratively, "speech"; and none knows the manner of that reaching save he, may peace be upon him, to whom it reached; and that he was as a copyist to whom [a text] is dictated and who writes it down — all of it: its chronicles, its narratives, and its laws — and for this reason he is called a "scribe" (*meḥoqeq*).

pairs.en: **The Eighth Principle**
the Torah sent down upon Moses
from the mouth of the Almighty
the manner of that reaching
as a copyist to whom [a text] is dictated
scribe

aligned.ja: ולא פרק בין ובני חם כוש ומצרים ופוט וכנען, ושם אשתו מהטבאל בת מטרד, או אנכי ה', ושמע ישראל ה' אלהינו ה' אחד, אלכל מפי הגבורה, ואלכל תורת ה' תמימה טהורה קדושה אמת.
aligned.en: There is no difference between "and the sons of Ham: Cush and Egypt and Put and Canaan" (Genesis 10:6) and "and his wife's name was Mehetabel the daughter of Matred" (Genesis 36:39), on the one hand, and "I am the Lord" and "Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one," on the other: all of it is "from the mouth of the Almighty," and all of it is "the Torah of the Lord, perfect, pure, holy — truth."

pairs.ja: ובני חם כוש ומצרים ופוט וכנען
pairs.en: the sons of Ham: Cush and Egypt and Put and Canaan
I am the Lord
all of it is "from the mouth of the Almighty,"

pairs.ja: תורת ה' תמימה טהורה קדושה אמת
pairs.en: the Torah of the Lord, perfect, pure, holy — truth

aligned.ja: ואנמא צאר מנשה ענדהם אשד כפר ונפאק מן כל כאפר לט'נתה אן פי אלתורה לב וקשר, ואן הד'ה אלתוארך' ואלאכ'באר לא פאידה פיהא ואנהא מן ענד משה, והו מעני אין תורה מן השמים.
aligned.en: Manasseh was, in their view, the most utterly unbelieving and faithless of all unbelievers, because he supposed that the Torah has a kernel and a husk, and that these chronicles and narratives are of no benefit and were [composed] by Moses [of his own accord]; and this is [the meaning of] "[one who says] the Torah is not from Heaven."

pairs.en: Manasseh was, in their view, the most utterly unbelieving and faithless of all unbelievers
the Torah has a kernel and a husk
the Torah is not from Heaven

aligned.ja: קאלוא הו אלד'י יעתקד אן כל התורה כולה מפי הגבורה חוץ מפסוק אחד שלא אמרו הקב"ה אלא משה מפי עצמו וזה הוא כי דבר בזה תעלי אללה ען קול אלכאפרין, בל כל חרף מנהא פיה אלחכם ואלעג'איב למן פהמה אללה, ולא תדרך גאיהֵ חכמתהא ארוכה מארץ מדה ורחבה מני ים.
aligned.en: [The Sages] said: he is one who believes that the whole Torah is "from the mouth of the Almighty" except for one verse, which (he claims) the Holy One, blessed be He, did not say, but Moses [said] of his own accord — and this is [the meaning of] "for he has despised the word of the Lord" (Numbers 15:31). God is exalted above the saying of the unbelievers! Rather, every letter of it contains wisdom and wonders for the one whom God has given to understand it; and the utmost of its wisdom cannot be apprehended — "longer than the earth is its measure and broader than the sea" (Job 11:9);

pairs.ja: כל התורה כולה מפי הגבורה חוץ מפסוק אחד
pairs.en: the whole Torah is "from the mouth of the Almighty" except for one verse
Moses [said] of his own accord

pairs.ja: כל חרף מנהא פיה אלחכם ואלעג'איב
pairs.en: every letter of it contains wisdom and wonders

pairs.ja: ארוכה מארץ מדה ורחבה מני ים
pairs.en: longer than the earth is its measure and broader than the sea

aligned.ja: וליס לאלאנסאן אלא אלחדו נחו דוד משיח אלהי יעקב אלד'י דעי גל עיני ואביטה נפלאות מתורתיך. וכד'לך תפסירהא אלמרוי הו איצ'א מפי הגבורה, והד'א אלד'י נעמלה אליום מן צפהֵ אלסוכה ואללולב ואלשופר ואלציצית ואלתפלים וגירהא הי בעינהא אלצפה אלתי קאל אללה למשה וקאל לנא, והו מוצל רסאלה נאמן פי תוצילה. ואלקול אלמדלול בה עלי הד'ה אלקאעדה אלת'אמנה הו קולה בזאת תדעון כי יי שלחני וכו' כי לא מלבי.
aligned.en: and a person has only to [follow] the way of David, the anointed of the God of Jacob, who prayed, "open my eyes that I may behold wonders out of Your Torah" (Psalms 119:18). So too its traditional interpretation is likewise "from the mouth of the Almighty"; and this which we practice today as to the form of the *sukkah*, the *lulav*, the *shofar*, the *tzitzit*, the *tefillin*, and the rest, is the very form that God told to Moses, and [Moses] told to us — and he is a faithful messenger in his delivery. The saying that indicates this eighth principle is, "By this you shall know that the Lord has sent me [to do all these works, and that it is not of my own heart]" etc. (Numbers 16:28).

pairs.en: open my eyes that I may behold wonders out of Your Torah
its traditional interpretation is likewise "from the mouth of the Almighty"

pairs.ja: צפהֵ אלסוכה ואללולב ואלשופר ואלציצית ואלתפלים
pairs.en: the form of the *sukkah*, the *lulav*, the *shofar*, the *tzitzit*, the *tefillin*
a faithful messenger in his delivery
By this you shall know that the Lord has sent me

aligned.ja: ואלקאעדה אלתאסעה אלנסך'. וד'לך אן הד'ה שריעהֵ משה לא תנסך' ולא תאתי שריעה מן קבל אללה גירהא, ולא יזאד פיהא ולא ינקץ מנהא לא פי אלנץ ולא פי אלתפסיר, קאל לא תוסף עליו ולא תגרע ממנו. וקד בינא מא ינבגי פי הד'ה אלקאעדה פי צדר הד'א אלתאליף.
aligned.en: **The Ninth Principle** — abrogation [denied]. That is, that this Law of Moses will not be abrogated, and no [other] Law will come from God besides it, and nothing will be added to it nor taken from it, neither in the text nor in the interpretation, as it is said, "you shall not add to it, nor diminish from it" (Deuteronomy 13:1). We have already set out what is fitting concerning this principle in the introduction to this work.

pairs.en: **The Ninth Principle** — abrogation [denied]
this Law of Moses will not be abrogated

pairs.ja: לא יזאד פיהא ולא ינקץ מנהא
pairs.en: nothing will be added to it nor taken from it

pairs.ja: לא פי אלנץ ולא פי אלתפסיר
pairs.en: neither in the text nor in the interpretation

pairs.ja: לא תוסף עליו ולא תגרע ממנו
pairs.en: you shall not add to it, nor diminish from it

aligned.ja: ואלקאעדה אלעאשרה אנה תעלי יעלם אפעאל אלנאס ולא יהמלהא. וליס כראי מן קאל עזב ה' את הארץ, בל כמא קאל גדול העצה ורב העליליה אשר עיניך פקוחות על כל דרכי בני האדם, וקאל וירא יי כי רבה רעת האדם בארץ, וקאל זעקת סדום ועמורה כי רבה, פהד'א ידל עלי הד'ה אלקאעדה אלעאשרה.
aligned.en: **The Tenth Principle** — that He, may He be exalted, knows the deeds of men and does not neglect them. (*Divine knowledge of human deeds*: that God knows and does not neglect the deeds of human beings.) [This is] not as the view of one who said, "the Lord has forsaken the earth" (Ezekiel 8:12); rather it is as [Scripture] said, "great in counsel and mighty in deed, whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of men" (Jeremiah 32:19), and "and the Lord saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth" (Genesis 6:5), and "the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah, because it is great" (Genesis 18:20). This indicates this tenth principle.

pairs.en: The Tenth Principle
knows the deeds of men and does not neglect them
the Lord has forsaken the earth

pairs.ja: עיניך פקוחות על כל דרכי בני האדם
pairs.en: whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of men
the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah, because it is great

aligned.ja: ואלקאעדה אלחאדיהֵ עשר אנה תעלי יג'אזי מן ימתת'ל אואמר אלתורה, ויעאקב מן ירתכב נואהיהא, ואן אעט'ם ג'זאה העולם הבא, ואשד עקאבה אלכרת, וקד קלנא פי הד'א אלפצל מא פיה כפאיה. ואלנץ אלמדלול בה עלי הד'ה אלקאעדה קולה אם תשא חטאתם ואם אין מחיני נא מספרך, וג'אובה תעלי מי אשר חטא לי, דליל עלי תחציל אלטאיע ואלעאצי ליג'אזי הד'א ויעאקב הד'א.
aligned.en: **The Eleventh Principle** — that He, may He be exalted, rewards the one who fulfills the commands of the Torah and punishes the one who commits its prohibitions; and that His greatest reward is the World to Come, and His severest punishment is *karet*. We have already said in this section what is sufficient on this. The text that indicates this principle is His saying, "if You will forgive their sin —; and if not, blot me out, I pray, from Your book" (Exodus 32:32), and His answer, may He be exalted, "whoever has sinned against Me, [him will I blot out of My book]" (Exodus 32:33) — a proof of the [exact] reckoning of the obedient and the disobedient, that He may reward this one and punish that one.

pairs.en: The Eleventh Principle
rewards the one who fulfills the commands of the Torah
His greatest reward is the World to Come
His severest punishment is *karet*

pairs.ja: אם תשא חטאתם ואם אין מחיני נא מספרך
pairs.en: if You will forgive their sin —; and if not, blot me out, I pray, from Your book
the [exact] reckoning of the obedient and the disobedient

aligned.ja: ואלקאעדה אלת'אניהֵ עשר ימות המשיח. והו אלאימאן ואלתצדיק במג'יה ולא יסתבטי אם יתמהמה חכה לו, ולא יצ'רב לה אג'ל ולא תתאול אלנצוץ לאכ'ראג' וקת מג'יה, אלחכמים יקולון תפוח דעתן של מחשבי קצין. ואן יעתקד פיה מן אלתעט'ים ואלמחבה ואלדעא לה עלי קדר מא ג'א פיה עלי ידי כל נבי מן משה אלי מלאכי.
aligned.en: **The Twelfth Principle** — the days of the Messiah. That is, the belief and affirmation that he will come, and not to deem him slow [in coming] — "though he tarry, wait for him" (Habakkuk 2:3) — and not to set a [fixed] term for him, nor to interpret the [scriptural] verses so as to extract a time for his coming. The Sages say, "may the spirit of those who calculate the [messianic] ends expire" (BT Sanhedrin 97b). And [one must] hold concerning him such reverence and love, and pray for him, in accordance with what has come [in prophecy] at the hand of every prophet from Moses to Malachi.

pairs.en: **The Twelfth Principle** — the days of the Messiah
the belief and affirmation that he will come

pairs.ja: לא יסתבטי אם יתמהמה חכה לו
pairs.en: not to deem him slow [in coming] — "though he tarry, wait for him"
may the spirit of those who calculate the [messianic] ends expire

pairs.ja: עלי ידי כל נבי מן משה אלי מלאכי
pairs.en: at the hand of every prophet from Moses to Malachi

aligned.ja: ומן אשך פיה או אסתקל אמרה כד'ב אלתורה אלתי ועדת בה בתצריח פי פרשת בלעם ואתם נצבים. ומן ג'מלהֵ הד'ה אלקאעדה אן לא מלך לישראל אלא מן דוד ומן נסל שלמה כ'אצה, וכל מן כ'אלף אמר הד'ה אלביתה כפר באללה ובנצוץ אנביאה.
aligned.en: Whoever doubts him or makes light of his matter gives the lie to the Torah, which promised him explicitly in the portion of Balaam (Numbers 24:17) and [in the portion] "You are standing this day" (Deuteronomy 30:3–5). Included in this principle is that there is no king for Israel except from [the house of] David and from the seed of Solomon in particular; and everyone who contests the [right of] this house has denied God and the words of His prophets.

pairs.en: gives the lie to the Torah, which promised him
the portion of Balaam

pairs.ja: לא מלך לישראל אלא מן דוד ומן נסל שלמה
pairs.en: there is no king for Israel except from [the house of] David and from the seed of Solomon
has denied God and the words of His prophets

aligned.ja: ואלקאעדה אלת'אלת'הֵ עשר תחיית המתים וקד בינהא.
aligned.en: **The Thirteenth Principle** — the resurrection of the dead; and we have already made it plain.

aligned.ja: למא אן קאל אינו חייב עד שיעשה בהן חבורה, תבין מן ד'לך אן המכה את המת פטור לאנה אינו בן חבורה חיניד', פטאבק עלי הד'א אלמעני זה חומר במקלל וכו'.
aligned.en:
#### Mishnah 1

Since [the Mishnah] said, "he is not liable until he makes in them a wound," you understand from this that one who strikes a corpse is exempt, since [the corpse] cannot be [made] subject to a wound at that point; and so the statement, "this is the stringency [in one case] as against [the case of] one who curses" etc., fits this sense.

pairs.ja: אינו חייב עד שיעשה בהן חבורה
pairs.en: he is not liable until he makes in them a wound
one who strikes a corpse is exempt
cannot be [made] subject to a wound
this is the stringency [in one case] as against [the case of] one who curses

aligned.ja: ור' יהודה יקול עד שישתמש בו שוה פרוטה. ואלחכמים יקולון כיון שנשתמש בו אפילו פחות משווה פרוטה. ואין הלכה כר' יהודה פי אלקולין. ולא כר' יוחנן בן ברוקה.
aligned.en: R. Yehudah says, "until he derives the value of a *perutah*'s benefit from it"; and the Sages say, "as soon as he has used it, even less than a *perutah*'s worth." The law is not in accordance with R. Yehudah in either of the two opinions, nor with R. Yoḥanan ben Beroka.

until he derives the value of a *perutah*'s benefit from it
the Sages say
less than a *perutah*'s worth

pairs.en: The law is not in accordance with R. Yehudah in either of the two opinions
nor with R. Yoḥanan ben Beroka

aligned.en:
#### Mishnah 2

The "rebellious elder" (*zaken mamre*) is one who says, "Thus did I expound and thus did my colleagues expound; thus did I learn and thus did my colleagues learn." And his statement, "if they have heard [a tradition], they tell them" means: those [members of] the court, if they have knowledge of that ruling and have heard the legal warrant for it, inform the rebellious elder and those who differed with him of what they possess, and they make known to them the truth and with whom it lies.

pairs.en: those [members of] the court

aligned.en: And if those [members of] the court have no knowledge of that matter, they ask those above them, until [the question] reaches the Great Court; and if the Great Court has some tradition on the matter, they teach them what they possess of the received tradition; and if they too have nothing on it, then they employ the legal analogies (*qiyāsāt*) known to them, until they — or the majority of them — agree that the ruling is such-and-such, and they so inform them; and it then becomes obligatory to comply. One who differs [in practice] from what they transmitted or derived by analogy is the "rebellious elder." God said, "according to the Torah which they shall teach you, and according to the judgment [which they shall tell you, you shall do]" (Deuteronomy 17:11) — and "this is the thing which they derive by analysis and to which reasoning leads them: God commanded us to act upon their word," which is His saying "you shall do"; then He said, "you shall not turn aside from the thing which they tell you, to the right or to the left" (Deuteronomy 17:11) — and this is the thing that is transmitted among them generation from generation, namely that they say "thus have we received," and for this reason He said "which they tell you," for in that [domain] they have only the report, that is, they inform you of the received tradition they possess.

pairs.en: the Great Court
the legal analogies (*qiyāsāt*)

aligned.en: [The elder] cannot be [adjudged] a "rebellious elder" liable to death until he issues a ruling contrary to theirs in matters learned by analogy or interpretation, "in a matter whose willful [violation entails] *karet* and whose inadvertent [violation entails] a sin-offering," or where his ruling leads to that. For example: he differs with them concerning a certain fruit, whether it is subject to *ʿorlah* or not, or concerning a certain kind of planting, whether *ʿorlah* applies to it or not — for such a dispute leads to "a matter whose willful [violation entails] *karet* and whose inadvertent [violation entails] a sin-offering": for one who betroths a woman with that produce — according to the view that holds it *ʿorlah*, she is not betrothed and one who has relations with her is exempt; but according to the view that holds it not *ʿorlah*, she is betrothed, and one who has relations with her [unlawfully] is, if inadvertent, liable to a sin-offering, and if willful, to *karet*. So too [a dispute over] whether this touched something impure or something pure leads, in the matter of the impurity of the Sanctuary and its holy things, to "a matter whose willful [violation entails] *karet* and whose inadvertent [violation entails] a sin-offering"; and so reckon the rest.

pairs.en: a matter whose willful [violation entails] *karet* and whose inadvertent [violation entails] a sin-offering
*ʿorlah*
the impurity of the Sanctuary and its holy things

aligned.en: This is a subtle matter requiring much skill, for a dispute, when traced through very many transmitted steps and through the actions accompanying it at each step or at some of them, may at the end of the matter lead to "a matter whose willful [violation entails] *karet* and whose inadvertent [violation entails] a sin-offering." So too if he differs with them in the interpretation of a received [law] in which there is no [room for] analogy, even though his ruling leads only to the prohibition of a negative or positive commandment, he is put to death inasmuch as he is a sectarian (*min*); and in [the matter of] the "five *totafot*" he becomes a rebellious elder even with respect to this particular positive commandment, for it has gathered conditions not found in others, as is made plain in the Talmud. We have already set out, in the introduction to this work of ours, principles useful in this chapter regarding our distinction between the interpretation that is received [by tradition] and that which is derived by analogy.

pairs.en: a sectarian (*min*)
the "five *totafot*"
the interpretation that is received [by tradition] and that which is derived by analogy

aligned.en: [The elder] cannot be [adjudged] a "rebellious elder" unless he is "a scholar who has reached [the level of issuing] instruction," whose word is heeded and who is entitled to issue rulings, as it is said, "if a matter be too hard for you" etc. (Deuteronomy 17:8) — [meaning] one from whom nothing is hidden save the strange and abstruse matter. But a "disciple who has not reached [the level of issuing] instruction" — to whom everything is [too hard] — does not [become a rebellious elder]. And his statement, "his stringency [results in] his leniency" [means]: because he is "a disciple who has not reached [the level of issuing] instruction," he is not permitted to issue rulings, even on the truth concerning which there is no dispute; so when he overstepped and issued a ruling on a matter under dispute, whose [presuming to rule] is the added stringency — being subject to two prohibitions, the prohibition of issuing rulings and the prohibition of [ruling on a matter of] dispute — he is exempted from death, and there came concerning this an opinion that he does not incur death.

pairs.en: a scholar who has reached [the level of issuing] instruction
a disciple who has not reached [the level of issuing] instruction
his stringency [results in] his leniency

aligned.en:
#### Mishnah 3

His statement "exempt" [refers to a case] where he acknowledges its [the commandment's] obligation upon him, but neglects it by way of disobedience — as it says, "to transgress the words of the Torah" — so long as he admits that it is a transgression; for this reason he does not incur court-imposed death, since one who [merely] neglects a positive commandment is not put to death. But if he said, "there is no [obligation of] *tefillin* upon me" by way of unbelief, he is put to death inasmuch as he is a sectarian (*min*), not inasmuch as he is a rebellious elder.

pairs.en: neglects a positive commandment
by way of unbelief
a sectarian (*min*), not inasmuch as he is a rebellious elder

aligned.en: This matter is exceedingly fine; for this point is liable to confuse many of the learned, who suppose that when [the Sages] say in the Talmud, concerning the rebellious elder, "he is not liable until he says such-and-such, and until he does such-and-such, and on such-and-such conditions," it means that whenever those conditions are not all fulfilled he goes free of [all] liability. But it is not so; rather its meaning is that he is not liable on the score of [being] a rebellious elder, and is exempt under the law of the rebellious elder — yet he may [still] deserve death on other grounds.

pairs.en: not liable on the score of [being] a rebellious elder
deserve death on other grounds

aligned.en: Consider: a man who says that his view and belief is the duality [of God] or the trinity — and this, beyond doubt, gives the lie to the saying of Scripture, "the Lord is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4) — shall we say that this one is not put to death, or that he is [merely] a rebellious elder? [Rather,] this one is put to death inasmuch as he has "gone out from the rule," that is, from the community of Israel, from whom come the sinners, one of whom — that is, one of the sinners — is the rebellious elder.

pairs.en: the duality [of God] or the trinity
gone out from the rule
the community of Israel

aligned.en: For the rebellious elder is not one who [seeks to] uproot the [whole] Law, nor one who at a single stroke gives the lie to the entire [body of] tradition, like the Sadducees and the Boethusians; rather he is a man who prefers his own opinion to the opinion of the Great Court, and Scripture imposed death upon him in order to magnify their right [to authority], just as Scripture imposed death upon one who curses his father, in order to magnify the right of his parents.

pairs.en: the Sadducees and the Boethusians
prefers his own opinion to the opinion of the Great Court
to magnify their right [to authority]

aligned.en: For this reason some of [the Sages] said: "[the death of] a rebellious elder is [only] by leave of the [Great] Court; should the court wish to forgive him, they forgive him" — but it is not so, for a reason they mentioned: "lest disputes multiply in Israel." As for the Sadducees and the Boethusians, who give the lie to the [entire] tradition at one stroke and confine themselves to the text of the Torah and their own interpretation of it, they are not of this category at all; rather they are of the category of those who say "the Torah is not from Heaven," as we explained in the tenth chapter of this tractate, where we set down the principles of the Law.

pairs.en: lest disputes multiply in Israel
the Torah is not from Heaven
the principles of the Law

aligned.en: Such men are put to death [precisely] for unbelief, just as one is put to death who denies the divine Lordship or who gives the lie to the prophecy of Moses; for everyone who demolishes one of those principles which I made plain to you has gone out from the rule of those who hold by the Law. I have prolonged this discourse only because in it, too, there are principles of belief of which not everyone has taken note.

pairs.en: denies the divine Lordship
gives the lie to the prophecy of Moses
principles of belief of which not everyone has taken note

aligned.en:
#### Mishnah 4

[The Mishnah] makes clear that [the rebellious elder] is put to death only by [the testimony of] witnesses and [after due] warning; for among all those liable to death or *karet* there is none who does not require warning except for the inciter (*mesit*) and the conspiratorial witnesses (*ʿedim zomemin*). For the [very] character of the inciter's case makes warning impossible with it, as is made plain in [chapter] seven; and likewise the conspiratorial witnesses — had we warned them, they would not have given their testimony, and the [very] existence of this law would be done away with, yet God brought it into being and decreed it. The law is in accordance with R. Akiva.

pairs.en: the inciter (*mesit*)
the conspiratorial witnesses (*ʿedim zomemin*)
The law is in accordance with R. Akiva

aligned.en:
#### Mishnah 5

"What he did not hear" — this means that he says [in God's name] what no revelation ever brought to him from God at all. "And what was not said to him" — this means that he claims [as his own] the prophecy of another, saying, "to me God spoke this speech," when it was not said to him but was said to another. We have already explained, in the introduction to this work of ours, the kinds of prophets among those who lay claim to prophecy, and how the true one is distinguished from the false. "And one who disobeys the words of a prophet" means that he is lax and slack toward the commands of the prophets and does not fulfill them with diligence and care.

aligned.en: God said: "And it shall come to pass that the man who will not hearken to My words" (Deuteronomy 18:19) — read it: "who is not heard" (*lo yishamaʿ*), "who does not hear" (*lo yishmaʿ*), "who does not let [others] hear" — the meaning of this being: one from whom [the prophet's words] are not heard [i.e., the disobedient]; or [the prophet] himself, if he does not let another hear what he was commanded to make heard; or [the prophet] himself, if he does not himself hear [obey] what he was commanded and rebels against his [own] prophecy — for all [of these], "I will require it of him" (Deuteronomy 18:19), and that is "death at the hand of Heaven." We have already explained, in chapter nine, what "death at the hand of Heaven" is.

#### Mishnah 6

His statement, "even though she has not [yet] been cohabited with" [means]: if she is a maiden, a virgin, you should not suppose that she is [subject to] stoning on account of her being a virgin; rather, from the moment she "entered the husband's domain" she has gone out from the category of "a betrothed maiden" and her law has become like the law of every married woman — [death] by strangulation. And it is established with us that one who has relations with the daughter of a priest [who has committed adultery] is [subject to death] by strangulation, like the law of [the adulterer with] every married woman: both she and he [are punished] by strangulation.

aligned.en: Scripture excluded the daughter of a priest from the general rule by its statement, "and the daughter of a man, a priest, when she profanes herself by playing the harlot" etc. (Leviticus 21:9) [— making her liable to burning], but her partner remained within the general rule. And [as for] those who conspire [falsely] against a priest's daughter, [their punishment] is reckoned according to her partner, not according to her, as it is said, "as he purposed to do to his brother" (Deuteronomy 19:19) — "to his brother," and not "to his sister"; that is, when the testimony embraces a man and a woman, one considers what would fall upon the man by their testimony, and that is what falls upon [the conspiring witnesses]. And this daughter of a priest — whether she was the wife of a priest or the wife of a *natin* or a *mamzer* — and [the point is] that this marriage involves a transgression, since she is a married woman: if she commits adultery, [she is liable] to burning.
